mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about the reactivity series of metals is a common misconception?

options.A: Metals higher in the series can displace metals lower in the series from their compounds.
options.B: All metals react vigorously with dilute acids.
options.C: Reactivity decreases down the group for alkali metals.
options.D: Gold is less reactive than copper.

mcqs.answer: All metals react vigorously with dilute acids.
mcqs.explanation: The reactivity series indicates that only metals above a certain position react readily with dilute acids. Many less reactive metals (e.g., copper, silver) show little or no reaction. Therefore statement B is a misconception. Options A, C and D are correct statements about the series.

mcqs.learning_point: Use metal reactivity to predict displacement
mcqs.question: When a strip of zinc metal is placed in a solution of copper(II) sulfate, which of the following correctly describes the reaction?

options.A: No reaction because both are metals.
options.B: Zinc displaces copper forming zinc sulfate and copper metal.
options.C: Copper displaces zinc forming copper sulfate and zinc metal.

mcqs.answer: Zinc displaces copper forming zinc sulfate and copper metal.
mcqs.explanation: Zinc is higher than copper in the reactivity series, so it can displace copper ions from copper(II) sulfate, producing ZnSO₄ in solution and metallic Cu as a solid. Option A ignores reactivity, C reverses the series, and D is unrelated to displacement reactions.

mcqs.question: Which of the following reactions is a double displacement (metathesis) reaction?
mcqs.explanation: In a double displacement reaction, the cations and anions of two compounds exchange partners. Reaction B shows Ag⁺ swapping with Na⁺, forming AgCl and NaNO₃. Reaction A is a single displacement, C is decomposition, and D is a single (metal) displacement.

mcqs.question: In which of the following reactions will a solid precipitate be formed?
mcqs.explanation: Barium sulfate (BaSO₄) is insoluble in water, so mixing BaCl₂ and Na₂SO₄ yields a white solid precipitate. The other combinations either produce soluble salts, water, or a gas, not a solid precipitate.

mcqs.question: Which of the following reactions is an example of a displacement reaction?
mcqs.explanation: Zinc, being more reactive than copper, displaces copper from copper(II) sulfate, producing zinc sulfate and copper metal. Option A is a combination reaction, C is dissociation, and D is decomposition.

mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly orders the metals from most to least reactive according to the reactivity series?
mcqs.explanation: In the reactivity series, magnesium is more reactive than iron, which in turn is more reactive than copper. Hence the correct order is Mg > Fe > Cu. The other options place the metals in incorrect order.

mcqs.learning_point: Use metal reactivity to predict displacement
mcqs.question: A displacement reaction is best defined as:

options.A: Two compounds exchanging ions to form two new compounds
options.B: An element replacing another element in a compound because it is more reactive
options.C: Decomposition of a compound into its elements
options.D: Combination of two elements to form a compound

mcqs.answer: An element replacing another element in a compound because it is more reactive
mcqs.explanation: A displacement (or replacement) reaction occurs when a more reactive element pushes out a less reactive element from its compound. Option A describes a double displacement, C describes decomposition, and D describes synthesis.

mcqs.question: Which of the following reactions is a double displacement reaction?
mcqs.explanation: In this reaction, the cations (Ca²⁺ and Na⁺) and anions (Cl⁻ and CO₃²⁻) exchange partners, forming calcium carbonate (a precipitate) and sodium chloride. This is the hallmark of a double displacement reaction. The other options are single displacement, combination, and ionisation respectively.
